explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/730: 'Are there infinitely many pairs of integers n ≠ m such that C(2n,n) and C(2m,m) have the same set of prime divisors?' (yes — even infinitely many consecutive pairs). The Lean statement asserts that S = {(n, m) : n < m ∧ primeFactors(centralBinom n) = primeFactors(centralBinom m)} is infinite; ordering n < m instead of n ≠ m only removes the symmetric duplicates and does not affect infinitude. Degenerate small values (centralBinom 0 = 1 has no prime factors, while centralBinom m ≥ 2 for m ≥ 1) cannot produce spurious pairs. Faithful.
